Is a directed edge in a MAG or PAG visible?

Source: R/queries.R
is_visible_edge.Rd

Checks whether the directed edge from --> to is visible (Zhang 2008, Definition 8): some node c not adjacent to to has either an edge into from, or a collider path into from whose non-endpoints are all parents of to.

Usage

is_visible_edge(cg, from = NULL, to = NULL, from_index = NULL, to_index = NULL)

Arguments

cg

A caugi object of class "AG" that is a MAG, or of class "PAG".

from, to

Node names. Use from_index/to_index to pass 1-based indices instead.

from_index, to_index

Optional 1-based indices, exclusive with from and to respectively.

Value

TRUE if the edge from --> to is visible, otherwise FALSE.

Details

In a MAG, from --> to means from is an ancestor of to in every DAG the MAG represents. The effect may run through latent variables, so it need not be direct. If the edge is visible, no represented DAG has an inducing path between from and to, relative to the latent variables, that is into from (Zhang 2008, Lemma 9). If it is invisible, some represented DAG has a latent common parent of the two (Lemma 10). Visibility therefore rules out latent confounding of the pair, not mediation. Maathuis and Colombo (2015) use it in their generalized back-door criterion.

In a PAG, an edge that meets the same criterion is definitely visible: it is visible in every MAG of the represented class (Zhang 2008, Section 4.2).

Only --> edges can be visible, so FALSE is returned for any other edge, for a non-adjacent pair and for the reverse of a directed edge.

References

Zhang, J. (2008). Causal reasoning with ancestral graphs. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 9, 1437-1474.

Maathuis, M. H. and Colombo, D. (2015). A generalized back-door criterion. The Annals of Statistics, 43(3), 1060-1088.

See also

Other queries: ancestors(), anteriors(), children(), components(), descendants(), districts(), edge_types(), edges(), exogenous(), is_acyclic(), is_admg(), is_ag(), is_caugi(), is_cpdag(), is_dag(), is_empty_caugi(), is_mag(), is_mpdag(), is_pag(), is_pdag(), is_simple(), is_ug(), m_separated(), markov_blanket(), neighbors(), nodes(), parents(), posteriors(), same_nodes(), spouses(), subgraph(), topological_sort()

Examples

# The `pcalg::visibleEdge()` example MAG.
mag <- caugi(A %-->% B, B %<->% C, B %-->% D, C %-->% D, class = "AG")
is_visible_edge(mag, "A", "B") # FALSE: every other node is adjacent to B
#> [1] FALSE
is_visible_edge(mag, "B", "D") # TRUE: A --> B with A, D non-adjacent
#> [1] TRUE
is_visible_edge(mag, "C", "D") # TRUE: collider path A --> B <-> C
#> [1] TRUE

pag <- caugi(A %-->% B, C %o->% A, D %o->% A, C %-->% B, class = "PAG")
is_visible_edge(pag, "A", "B") # TRUE: D *-> A with D, B non-adjacent
#> [1] TRUE
is_visible_edge(pag, "C", "B") # FALSE
#> [1] FALSE
